headline: High: Chatwoot’s broad egress and customer-data handling create default leakage/compliance risk; awesome-python adds no protective boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default injection bridge is documented. awesome-python is a non-runnable collection with no I/O surfaces, while chatwoot has broad egress but no cited path showing it ingests awesome-python outputs as instructions. The pair lacks a shared channel in the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, reassess injection risk.
IF chatwoot begins parsing content from awesome-python as instructions, the pathway becomes active.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy outputs from one agent into the other without review.
Disable any shared clipboard or message bus.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, messages, and reports, and has broad network egress. awesome-python is non-runnable and touches no data, so it does not add a leak path, but it also provides no containment. The default risk is chatwoot exfiltrating sensitive customer data to external services.
conditions: IF chatwoot sends customer records to any external integration or API, leakage occurs.
IF the pair is deployed on a shared workspace with exported logs, customer data may be copied into logs or reports.
mitigations: Disable unused integrations in chatwoot.
Review outbound destinations for customer-data fields.
Turn off verbose logging for customer records.
Separate customer-data workspaces from general tooling.
requires-engineering: add DLP or field-level redaction before egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. awesome-python is not runnable and has no permissions or filesystem/network write capability, while chatwoot exposes API integrations but no shared mutable resource with awesome-python is shown. Without a shared writable target, conflict is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk becomes active.
IF chatwoot is configured to write into a workspace also modified by another agent, reassess.
mitigations: Keep write targets separate.
Avoid shared git working trees.
Restrict chatwoot integrations to read-only where possible.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where awesome-python’s output becomes authoritative input to chatwoot. awesome-python is a static collection, and chatwoot is a support system with integrations, so the pair does not show a default automation chain. Any cascade would require an unusual manual bridge or custom integration.
conditions: IF a human or script copies content from awesome-python into chatwoot without verification, cascading error becomes possible.
IF chatwoot is configured to act on imported text from the collection, the risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before importing content.
Label imported content as untrusted.
Use a staging queue for any copied material.
requires-engineering: add validation before chatwoot actions.

E_compliance.rationale: chatwoot processes customer data and related records, which can carry privacy and retention obligations; awesome-python is a non-runnable open-source collection and does not itself add a compliance burden. The pair’s risk is driven by chatwoot’s handling of regulated customer information and external integrations, not by awesome-python.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is stored in chatwoot, retention and access controls must be enforced.
IF chatwoot integrations export customer data to third parties, residency or DPA checks are required.
mitigations: Review retention settings in chatwoot.
Confirm DPA and residency terms for each integration.
Limit access to customer records.
Export and delete test records after validation.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention enforcement.
